name: LLMLingua (Coarse-to-Fine Prompt Compression)
executive_summary: Compress a long prompt by up to 20x with little performance loss, using a budget controller and token-level iterative removal of low-information tokens — a general alternative to trimming content by hand.
description: Targets the growing-prompt-length problem directly: as CoT and in-context-learning prompts get longer (sometimes tens of thousands of tokens), inference cost and latency grow with them. LLMLingua uses a small language model to estimate each token's information content, a budget controller to decide how aggressively to compress different parts of the prompt while preserving semantic integrity, and a token-level iterative algorithm that models dependence between tokens rather than dropping them independently. Distinct from Chain-of-Density (which compresses by rewriting/densifying content) — LLMLingua compresses by removing low-information tokens from an existing prompt, applicable to any prompt type, not specifically summaries.
when_to_use: Long prompts (extensive few-shot exemplars, long retrieved context, long conversation history) where inference cost/latency is a binding constraint and some compression can be tolerated.
when_not_to_use: Short prompts already well within budget — compression overhead isn't worth it.
Prompts where every token is load-bearing and no semantic loss is acceptable (e.g. exact legal or medical text that must be preserved verbatim).
known_pitfalls: Aggressive compression ratios trade off against fidelity; the budget controller needs tuning per use case rather than a single universal compression ratio being safe everywhere.

primary_source.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
